title: Vulva anatomy: external structures and blood supply
description: Study the external vulva on a surface illustration: mons, labia, clitoral glans, vestibule, urethral opening and vaginal opening; deep structures remain unpinned.

questions.question: What structures are included in the vulva?
questions.answer: The vulva is the external genital region: mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoral structures and the vestibule with urethral and vaginal openings. Some deeper glands, vessels and nerves are described separately.

questions.question: Are the vulva and vagina the same structure?
questions.answer: No. The vulva refers to external genital anatomy; the vagina is an internal muscular canal extending from the cervix to the vaginal opening. The opening lies within the vulvar vestibule.

questions.question: How are the urethral and vaginal openings positioned?
questions.answer: The external urethral opening is typically inferior to the clitoral glans and superior to the vaginal opening within the vestibule. Their appearance varies normally, so a teaching illustration is not a diagnostic reference.

questions.question: What do the labia minora do?
questions.answer: The labia minora are inner hairless folds that border the vestibule and join anteriorly near the clitoral hood. Their size, color and asymmetry vary normally between people.

questions.question: Can the surface image show Bartholin glands or the clitoral crura?
questions.answer: No. The greater vestibular glands and most clitoral erectile structures lie below the surface. Their locations are described as deep study notes, not marked as visible on the external surface illustration.
